abstract: We present the development of a Named Entity Recognition (NER) dataset for Tagalog. This corpus helps fill the resource gap present in Philippine languages today, where NER resources are scarce. The texts were obtained from a pretraining corpora containing news reports, and were labeled by native speakers in an iterative fashion. The resulting dataset contains ∼\sim7.8k documents across three entity types: Person, Organization, and Location. The inter-annotator agreement, as measured by Cohen’s κ\kappa, is 0.81. We also conducted extensive empirical evaluation of state-of-the-art methods across supervised and transfer learning settings. Finally, we released the data and processing code publicly to inspire future work on Tagalog NLP.

bibliographic.title: Developing a Named Entity Recognition Dataset for Tagalog
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop in South East Asian Language Processing

content.problem: Tagalog lacks reliable named entity recognition resources because existing datasets contain noisy silver-standard annotations, narrow domain labels, or restricted access.
content.proposed_solution: The author created TLUnified-NER, a publicly available gold-standard dataset of 7.8k news documents annotated across three entity types by native speakers, and provided baseline benchmarks.
dataset_testbed: TLUnified-NER (new gold-standard dataset curated and annotated by the authors)
TLUnified pretraining corpus (source of news texts)
WikiANN Tagalog portion (reannotated test set used for cross-dataset comparison)

content.claim: TLUnified-NER provides a high-quality gold-standard Tagalog dataset where context-sensitive transformer models achieve over 90 F1 and outperform models trained on noisy silver annotations.
author_stated_limitations: The dataset has limited domain coverage because it consists primarily of news reports.
The benchmarks only evaluate a transition-based parser rather than other model architectures like conditional random fields.

evidence.problem_quote: Despite this fact, there are little to no resources for Tagalog [Cruz and Cheng (2022)](#bib.bib11 ""), hampering the development of reliable language technologies.
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: In this paper, we present TLUnified-NER,11 1 The dataset is accessible at [https://huggingface.co/datasets/ljvmiranda921/tlunified-ner](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ljvmiranda921/tlunified-ner "") a Tagalog dataset for Named Entity Recognition (NER). The texts were obtained from TLUnified [Cruz and Cheng (2022)](#bib.bib11 ""), a pretraining corpora containing news reports and other types of text.
evidence.claim_quote: Our iterative annotation process, together with our inter-annotator agreement, shows that the corpus is of high quality. In addition, our benchmarking results suggest that the task is learnable even with a simple baseline method.
author_stated_limitation_quotes: The TLUnified-NER corpora is comprised mostly by news reports. Although the texts demonstrate the standard usage of Tagalog, its domain is limited.
In addition, we only trained a transition-based parser model for our NER classifier. In the future, we plan to extend these benchmarks and include CRFs or other tools such as Stanford Stanza.
